newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Compromise unlikely in Midopa issue - Shindongbang.
newsitem.headline: Compromise unlikely in Midopa issue - Shindongbang.

text.p: A possible takeover bid for Midopa Department Store Co by Shindongbang Corp was unlikely to be settled through compromise, a senior Shindongbang official said on Thursday.
"Chances that both parties can settle the issue through compromise looks bleak," Kim Jin-il, a director of the nation's largest edible oil company, told Reuters by telephone.
"Our stance on wanting to participate in Midopa's management has not changed," Kim added.
He denied local newsports that chairmen of Shingdongbang and Dainong Corp met to settle the takeover issue. Dainong is the parent company of the department store.
"It's true the two chairmen met but they didn't specifically discuss a resolution of the takeover bid," he said. Dainong officials were not immediately available to comment.
Midopa came under spotlight after Shindongbang told the Korea Stock Exchange last week it was considering taking over the retailer.
If realised, it would be South Korea's first major hostile takeover.
The Federation of Korean Industries, which represents the interests of leading conglomerates, said on Tuesday it opposed any hostile takeover bid and would likely intervene in the Midopa issue.
Shindongbang, with its joint venture Dongbang Peregrine, currently holds a 6.74 percent stake in the retailer.
Shindongbang asked a Seoul court to prevent Midopa from issuing equity-linked bonds.
The company also asked the court to nullify last Friday's issuance by Midopa of 50 billion won worth of bonds with warrants and the exercising right by underwriters.
Shindongbang also demanded the court prevent any attempt by Midopa from selling Dainong shares. "We will raise the issues in a shareholders meeting," Kim said.

The company has urged Midopa to hold a shareholders meeting to question the retailer's management over excess payment guarantees to Dainong and attempt to sell its parent company's shares, which could damage Midopa assets.

Midopa's shares have begun to recover from recent lows. It hit the third-largest trading volume of the morning with 400,160 shares changing hands. It shed 2,200 won to 27,700, just off a limit low of 27,600 won.
